reel2.caption:
When you get busy, the first thing to disappear is the work that finds you new customers. That is why so many businesses go quiet.

Give it a fixed slot every day, even 30 minutes: follow up on quotes, message past customers, ask for reviews and referrals.

slides.sub: A calm 6 step check before you decide. Swipe.

slides.title: Check the demand
slides.head: Are you turning work down?
slides.body: Do customers come back or refer others? Has income been steady for several months, not just one lucky month?

slides.title: Know your numbers
slides.head: Living costs minus business profit.
slides.body: Add up your real monthly costs. The gap between that and what the business earns is what you must cover.

slides.title: Build a cushion
slides.head: Save for the slow months.
slides.body: Decide how many months of costs you want covered before you leave a salary, plus a buffer for the business.

slides.title: Count what you lose
slides.head: Medical aid, retirement, steady pay.
slides.body: Work out how you will replace what matters to you, or plan to go without.

slides.title: Have systems ready
slides.head: Quote, invoice, collect, record.
slides.body: These matter far more when the business is your only income.

slides.title: Go gradual, have a plan B
slides.head: Cut hours first if you can.
slides.body: Decide now what you will do if income drops. It makes the decision less scary.

carousel.caption:
Leaving a job is a big decision. A calm checklist beats excitement or frustration.

Six steps: check the demand, know your numbers, build a cushion, count what you lose, get your systems ready, and go gradual with a plan B. Read your employment contract before you resign.
